sections.h2: What should a seller know about West Virginia before choosing a local guide?
sections.html:
West Virginia is a small state with 55 counties, and most of the rules a seller meets are set statewide while the people who apply them sit in the county courthouse. The state had 1,793,716 residents at the 2020 census, a 3.2 percent drop from 2010, according to Wikipedia's state summary of Census figures.

That split between state rules and county offices shapes every guide on this site. The county assessor values the property, the sheriff sends and collects the tax ticket, the county clerk records the deed, and the county commission sits as the board that hears assessment protests. The city guides and county guides linked from this page each add the local detail on top of what is below.

sections.h2: How is West Virginia laid out, and where do sellers cluster?
sections.html:
West Virginia is the 10th-smallest state by area and the 12th-least populous. Its capital, Charleston, is also its most populous city, and Charleston is the county seat of Kanawha County, which had 172,381 residents in the 2020 census according to Wikipedia's county list.

The state's shape creates distinct corners. The northern panhandle sits between Pennsylvania and Ohio, and Wheeling and Weirton lie just across the border from the Pittsburgh area. Huntington, in the southwest, is close to Ohio and Kentucky. Martinsburg and Harpers Ferry, in the eastern panhandle between Maryland and Virginia, are considered part of the Washington metropolitan area.

The state is noted for mountains and rolling hills, along with a history of coal mining and logging. Railroad expansion opened the southern and northern coalfields to large-scale development, and by the early twentieth century West Virginia had become one of the leading coal producers in the country.

  • Charleston and the Kanawha Valley in the center of the state.
  • Huntington and the Ohio River corridor in the southwest.
  • Wheeling and Weirton in the northern panhandle.
  • Martinsburg and Harpers Ferry in the eastern panhandle.

sections.h2: How does property tax work across West Virginia?
sections.html:
Property tax is set locally but runs on one statewide calendar. The Tax Division says ownership, use and value are determined as of July 1 each year for the next calendar tax year, and that county sheriffs issue the tickets on or after July 15.

Taxes can be paid in two installments. Section 11A-1-3 makes the first payable September 1 and delinquent October 1, and the second payable March 1 and delinquent April 1. A two and one-half percent discount applies to payments made on or before the payable dates, and nine percent annual interest is added from the delinquency date on late payments.

The state Constitution divides property into four classes. Class II covers owner-occupied residential property used exclusively for residential purposes and farm land used for agriculture. Class III covers other property outside a municipality, and Class IV covers other property inside a municipality. Levies come from county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State, so the total bill reflects several taxing bodies.

The Tax Division also publishes a directory of the county assessors with all 55 offices, phone numbers and websites. Our homestead exemption guide covers the $20,000 exemption for owners who are 65 or older or disabled.

sections.h2: How do assessment protests and appeals work?
sections.html:
An owner who disagrees with an assessed value files a protest with the county commission, which sits as a board of equalization and review. The Tax Division says that board begins meeting for this purpose on February 1 each year, before the property taxes are due, may adjourn any time after February 15 if its work is done, and must adjourn no later than February 28.

Disputes over classification or taxability follow a different path. When the owner and the assessor disagree about the class or whether property is taxable, section 11-3-24a lets the question go to the Tax Commissioner, who must issue a ruling by the end of February of the tax year. Requests go through the county assessor in time to meet that date.

sections.h2: What are the costs and steps of transferring a deed in West Virginia?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the county clerk for recording, and the transfer tax is due then. Section 11-22-2 imposes an excise tax of $1.10 for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, on everyone who delivers, accepts or presents a document for recording.

The statute says only one state tax and one county tax is paid on a given document, collected in the county where the document is first admitted to record. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the document without the tax paid, and for trustee transfers or a clerk's conveyance of land sold for taxes, the grantee pays. A separate county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 has existed since 1968, and a county may raise it up to $1.65 per $500 under the statute. The statute also says that beginning July 1, 2025 the first excise tax is retained by the county where it was collected.

Because county rates can differ, a seller should call the clerk of the county where the property sits and ask the total transfer tax for the sale price before signing a contract.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about inheritance, probate and estate tax?
sections.html:
Estates start at the county level. The personal representative of a decedent who had nonprobate personal property files a sworn nonprobate inventory with the clerk of the county commission or the fiduciary supervisor within 90 days of qualifying, under section 11-11-7.

A state estate tax exists in Chapter 11, article 11, but it applies only when a federal estate tax is payable. For people who died in 2026, the IRS says the federal return is required when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific exemption is more than $15,000,000. Our estate and inheritance tax guide walks through the filing deadlines and what heirs owe when they sell.

The heir's own tax picture comes from basis. The IRS says basis in inherited property is generally the fair market value on the date of death, so a prompt sale usually produces little gain.

sections.h2: What are the landlord and tenant rules for selling a rental?
sections.html:
An owner who wants a tenant out goes to magistrate court or circuit court. Section 55-3A-1 allows a verified petition for unpaid rent, breach of a warranty or leasehold covenant, or damage to the property, and the court sets a hearing 5 to 10 judicial days after filing.

If the tenant does not respond, the court enters an order granting immediate possession. If the tenant answers, the hearing covers the defenses, and the order sets a vacate date after which the sheriff removes the tenant. Periodic tenancies can be ended with notice for one full period under section 37-6-5. Our eviction notice guide covers the steps and the day counts in more detail.

  • Magistrate court or circuit court in the county of the property.
  • Hearing 5 to 10 judicial days after the petition.
  • Sheriff removes a tenant who stays past the court's date.

sections.h2: Which West Virginia counties and cities have their own guide here?
sections.html:
The directory above this text links five city guides and fourteen county property tax guides. The cities are Charleston, Huntington, Morgantown, Parkersburg and Wheeling. The counties are Kanawha, Raleigh, Cabell, Berkeley, Greenbrier, Fayette, Hancock, Jefferson, Wood, Marion, Nicholas, Preston, Barbour and Harrison.

Not every town has its own page. If your house is in a county or city that is not listed, the statewide rules on this page still apply, and the county assessor and county clerk are the people to ask about local details. We buy houses in West Virginia as-is, with no commission and no closing costs to the seller, and you can call or text to ask about a specific property.

faqs.q: How many counties does West Virginia have?
faqs.a: West Virginia has 55 counties. The Tax Division's property tax directory lists an assessor for each of them, and each county also has its own sheriff, clerk and county commission.

faqs.q: When are West Virginia property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two installments. The first is payable September 1 and delinquent October 1, and the second is payable March 1 and delinquent April 1. Paying by the payable date earns a two and one-half percent discount, and late payments accrue nine percent annual interest.

faqs.q: What is the West Virginia transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $1.10 for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, payable when the deed is presented for recording. A county may also levy an additional excise tax. The grantor usually pays, and the county clerk can tell you the combined amount.

faqs.q: How is a West Virginia home assessed for tax?
faqs.a: At 60 percent of fair market value, as of July 1 each year. Owner-occupied residential property falls in Class II. A home owner who is 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled may claim a $20,000 homestead exemption by December 1.

faqs.q: Is there a West Virginia estate tax?
faqs.a: Chapter 11, article 11 of the Code imposes an estate tax, but section 11-11-3 applies it only when a federal estate tax is payable. For 2026 deaths the federal return is required above $15,000,000. Most families selling an inherited house are well below that.

faqs.q: Does this directory cover every West Virginia town?
faqs.a: No. It links five city guides and fourteen county guides. For a place that is not listed, the state rules above still apply, and the county assessor and clerk are the best local contacts.
